# wearable-hardware

Intro paragraph.

## Selection contract

<!-- Read by packages/research-enrich to judge whether a document belongs in this topic. English on purpose. -->

- **Purpose:** Determine which body-worn or equipment-mounted sensing hardware can capture motion and impact, and which sensing, materials, power, radio, sync, fabrication and optical methods from any field transfer onto a body or a piece of equipment.
- **Core:** IMUs and high-g or piezo impact sensing; textile and skin attachment; batteries, PMICs, and harvesting; BLE clocks and on-body antennas; firmware; enclosures and flexible or printed circuits; elastomers, hydrogels, liquid metal, and e-textiles; camera or event-camera ball spin and trajectory.
- **Adjacent (keep):** Wearable health and physiological sensing hardware (ECG, cardiac, sweat, glucose, electrodermal and pulse sensors, skin electrodes, smart textiles), because their materials, attachment, power and radio methods transfer. Visual-inertial odometry, event-camera SLAM and UWB or radio localization, because the sensor fusion transfers to IMU and optical tracking. Sparse IMU pose estimation; Apple Core Motion and watch batch sensors; sports biomechanics studies that report what a sensor must capture (stroke, serve, swing, impact); ball-material and approval tests.
- **Collected on purpose:** Vendor datasheets and SDK pages (ST, TDK, Bosch, Nordic, TI, Bluetooth, Zephyr, Gore, antenna notes) and open papers that transfer a sensing, power, radio, materials, or fabrication method onto a body or a piece of equipment.
- **Out of scope:** Clinical, biological or behavioral studies whose contribution is an endpoint, treatment or cohort result with no sensing, materials, power, radio or fabrication method; vehicle, building or robot navigation that uses no IMU, event camera or radio-localization method; sports-product market surveys with no hardware detail.
